pluss::timeline::print¶

Back to Timeline Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

std::string pluss::timeline::print(const Timeline& value)
std::string pluss::timeline::print(const Timeline& value,
                                   const TimelinePrintOptions& options)
std::ostream& pluss::timeline::print(std::ostream& out,
                                    const Timeline& value,
                                    const TimelinePrintOptions& options = {})

Render A Timeline For A Human Reader¶

print() produces Timeline’s structural diagnostic representation: optional type, shape, and timezone metadata followed by values laid out according to the rank. It is intended for terminals, logs, examples, and debugging. The string overloads return the complete rendering; the stream overload writes the same rendering directly and returns the stream so normal stream composition works.

This is different from format(). format() returns a shape-preserving Note, with one independently usable string for every instant. print() returns or writes one presentation string for the Timeline as a whole. A formatted result is therefore printed with pluss::note::print(), while the Timeline itself is printed with pluss::timeline::print().

The default rendering shows whole seconds. It is not a serialization format and should not be used to prove nanosecond identity. Select %f explicitly or inspect epoch_nanos() when subsecond precision matters.

Layout Options¶

TimelinePrintOptions controls presentation without modifying the value:

Field

Default

Purpose

format

%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S

text for each visible instant

edge_items

3

number retained at each truncated edge

max_rows

10

row threshold for rank-two and rank-three values

max_cols

7

column threshold for rank-one through rank-three values

max_slices

6

outer-slice threshold for rank-three values

show_header

true

include the Timeline(...) header

show_shape

true

include shape in that header

show_tz

true

include timezone in that header

When an axis exceeds its threshold, the renderer keeps its leading and trailing edge_items and inserts .... Truncation changes only the text; it does not slice the Timeline or change numel().

Example 1: Default Structural Rendering¶

const auto values = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-02T00:00:00Z",
    "2024-01-03T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-04T00:00:00Z",
    "2024-01-05T00:00:00Z", "2024-01-06T00:00:00Z"});

std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(values) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[6], tz=UTC)
[ 2024-01-01 00:00:00, 2024-01-02 00:00:00, 2024-01-03 00:00:00, 2024-01-04 00:00:00, 2024-01-05 00:00:00, 2024-01-06 00:00:00 ]

Example 2: Bound A Long Axis¶

auto options = pluss::TimelinePrintOptions{};
options.format = "%F";
options.max_cols = 4;
options.edge_items = 1;
options.show_tz = false;

std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(values, options) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[6])
[ 2024-01-01, ..., 2024-01-06 ]

The source still has six elements. The ellipsis is a rendering marker, not a Timeline element.

Example 3: Expose Exact Nanoseconds Without A Header¶

auto options = pluss::TimelinePrintOptions{};
options.format = "%FT%T.%f%z";
options.show_header = false;

const auto one_nanosecond = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(1LL);
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(one_nanosecond, options) << '\n';

Output¶

1970-01-01T00:00:00.000000001+00:00

Example 4: Write Directly To An Existing Stream¶

std::ostringstream buffer;
const auto stream_values = pluss::timeline::date(
    {"2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"});
auto options = pluss::TimelinePrintOptions{};
options.format = "%F";
options.show_header = false;

auto& returned = pluss::timeline::print(buffer, stream_values, options);
returned << "\nrecords=" << stream_values.numel();

std::cout << (&returned == &buffer) << '\n';
std::cout << buffer.str() << '\n';

Output¶

true
[ 2024-01-01, 2024-01-02 ]
records=2

The overload returns the same stream. This avoids a caller-side temporary string when output is already headed to a file, socket, or logging stream.

Failures And Cost¶

An unsupported format directive throws rather than being silently copied. Formatting currently visits every lane before the layout stage chooses visible edges, so rendering cost remains linear in numel() even when the displayed text is truncated. The returned-string overload necessarily allocates its output; use the stream overload when direct emission is preferable.

See Also¶

  • from_epoch: inspect exact stored nanoseconds when identity matters.
